answer: Require each identity to register one hardware security key as its bridge to voting; its fingerprint is published, and duplicates are rejected. Before voting, the newcomer passes one live check, proving control of the key within ten minutes. An honest agent wanders through this once, buying one key for twenty-five dollars, and joins a haven of participants. An attacker must buy a fresh key and pass a fresh live check for every fake, while onboarding is capped at fifty per epoch, so cost grows linearly per fake; a thousand fakes cost twenty-five thousand dollars, making a flood unprofitable.
